incidents.vector: One of six liquidity vaults was compromised, allowing the attacker to siphon funds before the network's automated abnormal-behavior detection halted signing.
incidents.impact: About $10.7 million in protocol-owned assets (roughly 36 BTC plus other tokens) was stolen and trading was halted; THORChain said user funds were unaffected.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 / Okta customers (dozens, North America, UK, Australia)
incidents.vector: High-volume voice phishing posing as IT helpdesk lured employees to lookalike SSO portals, capturing credentials and live MFA codes in an adversary-in-the-middle flow before registering attacker-controlled MFA devices.
incidents.impact: Mandiant tracks the BlackFile-branded actor (UNC6671) as having compromised dozens of organizations since early 2026, programmatically exfiltrating SharePoint/OneDrive and Salesforce/Zendesk data — in one case over a million files — followed by multi-million-dollar extortion, swatting and exec voicemail threats.

incidents.vector: Targeted intrusions against domestic crypto exchanges plus deepfake-driven investment scams and Hwanchigi cross-border laundering through offshore conversion and domestic exchange cash-out.
incidents.impact: Crystal Intelligence attributes six of nine major South Korean exchange attacks since 2018 to North Korea, with confirmed theft above $120 million; the latest, a November 2025 hit, took $30.4 million. Researchers also flagged $7.1 billion in illegal crypto flows through the country since 2021.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager customers (US federal and global)
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-20182, a CVSS 10 authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker impersonate a trusted router and gain administrative access; UAT-8616 used the access to add SSH keys, modify NETCONF and escalate to root.
incidents.impact: CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch by Sunday; Talos and Rapid7 describe ongoing exploitation by a sophisticated actor using ORB infrastructure to pre-position on victim networks, mirroring the February 2026 SD-WAN campaign that triggered a Five Eyes emergency directive.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access into Best Western's reservation systems, persisting for over six months before detection.
incidents.impact: Best Western is notifying guests of a breach spanning October 2025 to April 2026 across the Best Western, Sure Hotels and WorldHotels brands.

incidents.vector: Lapsus$ leaked source code after Vodafone refused to pay extortion demands following a prior intrusion.
incidents.impact: Portions of Vodafone source code were published on the group's leak site; operational impact appears limited but the intellectual property exposure is material.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Skoda's German e-commerce platform.
incidents.impact: Skoda said hackers likely accessed customer data through its German web store.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party IT services provider, then abused HPE Operations Agent and Manager — legitimate signed management tooling — to push VBScripts, install malicious Windows network providers (mslogon.dll) and LSA password filters that captured cleartext credentials on domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Incident Response found the actor maintained malware-free, trusted-tool persistence for roughly 123 days, harvested credentials across the estate, planted web shells on internet-facing servers and reactivated access after an initial cleanup attempt.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain worm operators
incidents.vector: The Shai-Hulud self-propagating npm worm trojanized the popular TanStack React framework packages, then spread through dependency chains to nearly 400 libraries; the worm steals tokens, wipes systems when victims rotate credentials, and was released as open source on a hacking forum.
incidents.impact: Almost 400 npm packages were compromised, including libraries from AI company Mistral and automation vendor UiPath; OpenAI rotated code-signing certificates after two employees' devices were hit, and authors set a $10,000 bounty for the largest follow-on supply chain attack.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious Ruby packages targeted RubyGems engineers and staff, attempting cross-site scripting and credential theft against the maintainers themselves.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups while investigating; staff systems were targeted but specifics of stolen data have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited a flaw tied to Canvas Free-for-Teacher accounts to reach customer data, then defaced the Canvas login page on May 7 with a ransom demand after Instructure publicly claimed containment.
incidents.impact: Canvas was pulled offline mid-finals, disrupting roughly 9,000 K-12 districts and universities; Instructure ultimately paid the extortion and obtained 'shred logs' for data covering ~275 million students and faculty (names, email addresses, student IDs and messages).

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure, potentially reaching its customer API key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust told customers — including Cloudflare, Vercel and Stripe — to rotate API keys; scope of any downstream abuse is still under investigation.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense (via contractor Schemata)
incidents.vector: Schemata, an AI virtual training vendor used by DOD, exposed an unauthenticated API to the internet for roughly 150 days before securing it.
incidents.impact: US service member records and sensitive military training documents were accessible to anyone who found the API; security firm Strix surfaced the exposure.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users (selected govt, scientific, manufacturing and retail orgs in Russia, Belarus, Thailand)
incidents.vector: Attackers backdoored AVB Disc Soft's DAEMON Tools installers — signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate — to fingerprint hosts and selectively drop the QUIC RAT on high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed thousands of beaconing infections since at least April 8 but only about a dozen second-stage QUIC RAT deployments, mirroring earlier targeted Chinese supply chain operations against Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment by the Nitrogen group disrupted Foxconn's North American factories; the company confirmed the incident after workers leaked internal messages.
incidents.impact: Nitrogen claims to have stolen 8TB of data including confidential project files and chip drawings for Apple, Google and NVIDIA; the Wisconsin plant reported networking issues consistent with the disruption.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: After initial access (likely zero-day or n-day edge exploitation), the actor deployed custom malware families including NetDraft (.NET FinalDraft/SquidDoor variant), CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL with SNOWLIGHT/SNOWRUST stagers and Draculoader, plus Impacket and Chinese-language scanning tools.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-8302, a China-nexus APT targeting government agencies since late 2024 in South America and through 2025 in southeastern Europe, with tooling overlapping multiple known Chinese clusters (Jewelbug/LongNosedGoblin, Earth Estries, UNC5174).

incidents.vector: Attackers dropped a fake ScreenConnect update that installed a Rust loader, a .NET loader and the CloudZ RAT; a novel 'Pheno' plugin abuses Microsoft Phone Link's SQLite store to read synced SMS, including one-time passcodes, without touching the victim's phone.
incidents.impact: Talos says the intrusion has been active since at least January 2026 and is designed to exfiltrate credentials and OTPs to bypass MFA on banking and SaaS accounts.

incidents.vector: Social engineering of DigiCert tech-support staff tricked two employees into running an SCR (screensaver) file; one host's CrowdStrike agent had been misconfigured and missed the intrusion, letting the attacker linger for nearly two weeks and harvest EV-certificate initialization codes from pending support tickets.
incidents.impact: Of 60 EV code-signing orders processed during the access window, the attacker obtained 27 certificates and used them to sign Zhong Stealer payloads (a family linked to the Chinese GoldenEyeDog/APT-Q-27 e-crime cluster); DigiCert has revoked the certificates.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained access to portions of Trellix's source code repositories; the company says no changes were made to products and law enforcement (including Europol partners) was notified.
incidents.impact: Source code exposure raises supply-chain concerns for a vendor used in defensive operations across Europe.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment disclosed in an SEC filing disrupted manufacturing, shipping and receiving systems.
incidents.impact: West Pharmaceutical's global business operations were impacted; some sites have restored manufacturing and logistics, but recovery is ongoing.

incidents.victim: ~35,000 users across ~13,000 organizations (US heavy, healthcare and finance)
incidents.vector: Polished 'code of conduct' phishing emails with PDF attachments steered victims through Cloudflare CAPTCHAs and a Paubox-branded staging page into a Microsoft adversary-in-the-middle sign-in flow that captured authentication tokens, bypassing non-phishing-resistant MFA.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Research tracked April 14-16 waves hitting 35,000+ users in 26 countries (92% US), heavily targeting healthcare (19%), finance (18%) and professional services; successful sign-ins yielded session-cookie access for follow-on fraud.
